A10.title: Work sessions: start and end buttons with a catch-up and blog ideas
A10.what:
Two Maintenance buttons for Blake's own work log, usable from phone or Mac.

**Start work session:** opens an issue "Work session N" (numbered automatically, label `work-session`; an open one means clocked in). Its first comment is a short catch-up that doesn't depend on how long it's been: the **last 8 merged pull requests** (button input, 5 to 10), each with its plain-words description; anything on `hold` or labeled `needs decision`; and the next `ready` issues.

**End work session:** finds the open session issue and posts everything since it was opened: pull requests merged, issues opened and closed, checks that failed and anything put on hold, compiled from the pull requests' own words (no AI writing). Then a short **Blog ideas** section written by the coordinator: a few topics drawn from that session's pull requests and reviews (problems hit, fixes found, decisions made), each with one or two suggested phrasings Blake can reuse. Clearly labeled as suggestions; no summary, no full drafts. Then the issue closes.

Later: each session also lands as a note in the vault (with A9), and sessions can be planned ahead ("session 3 = tasks 6 to 10") by attaching issues.

Reuse: the weekly update script's date-range report (#101) and the Agents workflow's Claude job (#121) for the blog ideas.
